entities.summary:
Ama-e was an Ancient Sumerian businesswoman who left a lasting legacy in the early history of trade and commerce.

Born in the Sumerian city of Uruk, Ama-e rose to prominence as a skilled merchant and entrepreneur in the 2nd millennium BCE. Her business acumen and strategic partnerships enabled her to expand her trade networks across Mesopotamia, establishing herself as one of the earliest recorded female business leaders in the ancient world.

Ama-e's impact extended beyond her own era, influencing the development of trade and commerce in the ancient Near East. Her success paved the way for future generations of women in business, demonstrating the potential for women to excel in male-dominated fields.

One of Ama-e's most enduring legacies is the Ama-e Code, a set of business principles and practices that she developed and codified during her lifetime. This code, which emphasized fair trade practices, customer service, and employee welfare, remains an important model for business leaders today.

Ama-e's life and work are a testament to the power of innovation and entrepreneurship, inspiring future generations of business leaders and entrepreneurs around the world.
